content.comment_body: Hello, Different backlight colors are available as a feature in [product_name] hardware. Where do I select or change this option? I have installed an upgrade for [product_name] engineering software (full version). Thank you. The display provides a modern design: • Six lines and 16 characters per line allow for double the display information, enabling clear message texts. • Enhanced display with clear operator details and improved readability; simplified menu operations and advanced diagnostics options. • Backlight colors including white, orange, and red can be selected, offering visual emphasis for alarms or alerts.
You can control the backlight colors using flags. If you activate flag 25, you get one color, flag 26 gives you another, and so on.
Hello, where do I find those flags? Are they set in the message text box?
Refer to the attached video for guidance.

The flags can be found in the same panel as digital inputs and outputs on the left side of your PC screen (Constants => Digital). The last option is M or Flag. Place a Flag on the worksheet, select it with your mouse, and right-click to change the flag number through Block Properties.
If you use backlight flags in your program, automatic activation of the white backlight with a keypress will no longer work.

Thanks, this helped! How do I keep the screen lit at all times? When using M functions, the light goes off until a menu is selected. I want the light to stay on and change color only when an event occurs. Thanks.

[user_name], When you control the backlight using M-bits in your program, the backlight will remain on only when any of the M-bits are active. Ensure at least one M-bit is always on to keep the backlight continuously lit. For instance, you could use a door sensor to detect if the panel door is open. Otherwise, the backlight will remain on even inside a closed cabinet.
How can I enable these for the default menus, time, and date screens?

For the system menu and related setup screens, once you assign a flag for backlight control in the [product_name] program, the automatic backlight activation on keypress does not work anymore. If settings need to be made in the system menu, the backlight stays off.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are searching for guidance on changing and controlling the display backlight color for [product_name] hardware via [product_name] engineering software. The main insights highlight that while the color-control feature exists, its configuration—especially with flags—is not straightforward, and there are side effects such as losing automatic backlight activation on keypress. Users find the functionality difficult to locate and want both continuous backlight and color changes based on events.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect an easy interface within the engineering software to select and manage the display backlight color, along with the ability to keep the screen illuminated at all times and dynamically change colors according to events.
